$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-DX-006 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §8.8 and the RF-DX-006 inventory entry. Expresses imaging/report-descriptor handling STRUCTURE only: externally reported TEXT descriptors (report/clinician/radiology) may contribute exact anatomy, classification, and tendon involvement according to anchor quality. Raw user-uploaded images cannot be interpreted by the language model and require a separately validated imaging subsystem. QRF-006 (bull's-eye descriptor) is reference-only and is not a stand-alone diagnosis, grade, or prognosis rule. Does not bypass RF-SAF-006. No rehab, dosage, progression, confidence, or return-to-sport logic; safety precedence preserved. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.

input_contract.$comment: Structural inputs taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §8.8. Only externally reported TEXT descriptors are handled; raw media is never interpreted here.

decision_contract.$comment: Report-descriptor handling structure only. Report text contributes structured fields according to anchor quality; it does not become unrestricted diagnosis/rehab/RTS clearance, numeric confidence, or probability, and does not bypass RF-SAF-006. No rehab authorization, no numeric values. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Mixed normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture refs and evidence claim preserved per source: architecture V3.1-6 (diagnosis anchor quality), V3.1-14.1 (media states), V3.1-25 (media-state hardening); QRF-006 (E1) used ONLY when the bull's-eye descriptor is specifically relevant. Per §8.8: report TEXT may contribute exact anatomy, classification, and tendon involvement according to anchor quality, but raw user-uploaded images cannot be interpreted by the language model and require a separately validated imaging subsystem (V3.1 §25 — the conversational model never interprets raw images/videos). Prohibited use preserved exactly: a bull's-eye descriptor is NOT a stand-alone diagnosis, grade, or prognosis rule, and BAMIC ontology evidence is not authority for media-source handling. The rule preserves uncertainty for unclear/partial/contradictory/user-entered-without-source/unsupported report language, does not generalize a specific descriptor beyond its permitted source scope, does not authorize rehab or return-to-sport, and does not bypass RF-SAF-006 when avulsion/full-thickness/postoperative/major-retraction/external-restriction descriptors appear. Diagnosis report-handling rule, not a safety rule, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty; safety precedence preserved. No diagnostic confidence model is authored here (deferred to the later confidence objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
